title: burnt $400 and made a World Cup simulator using Fable. Here's what I got.
author: Puzzleheaded_Act5292
selftext:
I know many people talked about one-shot build. Here's one that took way longer.

I burnt about $400 on Fable and built a World Cup narrative simulator. Real football rules underneath blend in with Shonen comic energy.

Mbappé is the first finished character. Seven more storylines are in progress, and Kane / England is already half-wired. Every character has real career stuff baked in. For Mbappé that's 2018 champion, 2022 final loss, 2024 transfer. So the run feels like his actual football life.

There are two tracks that keep fighting each other. World Cup is the team goal. Ballon d'Or is the personal one. You're constantly balancing choices across different stats for both. Chase the World Cup, or chase the Ballon? If Mbappé carries alone, his numbers go up and France as a whole starts looking worse. Trust the squad and the trophy gets closer, but the Ballon case gets a lot less certain. That tension is the fun part.

Since the tone is shonen, I built a death dictionary that maps football events into that language:

* Elimination = snap dust. Final whistle, half the team just "disappears"
* Missed penalty = dies on that exact kick, with a clear killer moment
* Injury / red card = accidental death. Forced off, teammates watching the back leave

On the art side I used two SFX sticker sets: English comic style (BOOM / POW / CRACK / WHOOSH / SWISH) and Japanese manga style (バキ / ドクン / ゴゴゴ / シーン). Transparent PNGs that stack onto comic panels. Honestly, getting this layer to fit ate a ridiculous amount of time.

My favorite part is the live match presentation. The UI is a flat pitch with dots for player positions and the ball path. When something big happens, manga SFX and comic panels pop over the pitch like a page going off. The engine has 30+ pitch presets (PITCH\_POS), from kickoff, corners, and free kicks to saves, clearances, and offside. Each one has its own ball and player coordinates.

There's also a free-text box mid-match. Type whatever, and an intent lexicon routes it:

* "pass to Dembélé" → FREE\_TEAM (team bias)
* "shoot it yourself" → FREE\_RISK (gamble bias)

Those choices actually change how the match plays out.

Let me know if you want to play. Or tell me who the third playable line should be after Kane.

comments.author: Alstroph
comments.body:
Yeah, it’s delusional and a bit telling when people think they one-shot a game. Unless you’re making something on the level of Pong, then you’re really just one-shotting a POC. 

Ive got a serious game project from pre-AI that’s currently on hold, more than 3000 hours of my own time invested and 30k usd for contractors. 

Last year I started a solo ai-assisted game dev project. After 800\~ hours, it feels like the equivalent of 5k\~ hours has been completed, but it’s still not done.

If the average indie game takes 10k\~ person hours to build without AI tools, and if we optimistically assume that AI tools are a 10x multiplier, then you’re still looking at 1k person hours of time investment required.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
I'm one month in creating my game, 20 million output tokens used (Claude Code), almost 400 github commits across 18 branches.  I don't even have a proper demo yet.  
I estimate another 4-6 months before I might have something ready to release.

replies.author: teamharder
replies.body:
I think it entirely depends on the type of game. 2d gets up and running far faster than 3d. Animations also eat up a ton of time, so genres heavy with animation take longer as well. Human made asset packs can cut down on that time a ton though.

I made a shoot em up that uses physical pieces for the spaceship and that took about 3 months for a complete project. 1.5-2 if I had focused on it the whole time.

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body: There's also a reason so many of these AI games use pixel or voxel art.  It's *much* easier to get AI to consistently pump that stuff out than it is well made illustration or 3d models.  Hell, voxels are literally just math, Claude can make *all* of your visualizations for you.

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body:
Also those images look like they're coming straight from something like ChatGPT/Gemini, which are watermarked from hell to breakfast and the licensing for commercial use is dubious at best depending on their terms.  

Great for dev art but if you did ever want to release commercially pretty much all of it would need to be redone with clear commercial licensing provenance.  Just something to be aware of.
